title: Friedlander–Milnor conjecture for Lie groups
statement:
Let $G$ be a Lie group. Regard $BG$ as the classifying space of the underlying discrete topological group, and let $BG^{\rm top}$ be the classifying space with its usual topology. The canonical map

$$
\psi:BG\longrightarrow BG^{\rm top}
$$

is induced by the identity on the underlying group. **Friedlander–Milnor conjecture.** The map $\psi$ induces isomorphisms on homology and cohomology with every finite abelian coefficient group. This is a comparison conjecture between discrete and topological classifying spaces of Lie groups.
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Lie-group category/component conventions require primary scope confirmation.
technical_disposition: Every Lie group and every finite abelian coefficient group; discrete-to-topological classifying-space comparison requires global homological machinery. No short uniform mechanism identified.

title: The $C^1$ unipotent Jacobian univalence conjecture
statement: Let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be a $C^1$ map, and let $J(f)$ denote its Jacobian matrix. A matrix is **unipotent** when all its eigenvalues are $1$. **The $C^1$ unipotent Jacobian univalence conjecture.** If $J(f)$ is unipotent, then $f$ is injective. The conjecture is known for $n=2$ and, if established for all $n$, would imply the Jacobian Conjecture. The paper notes that the stronger bijectivity version has no known counterexample.
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Unipotence must hold at every point, not at one Jacobian.
technical_disposition: All dimensions and all C1 maps with pointwise unipotent Jacobian. Spectral information is local; integrating Jacobians does not preserve nilpotence. No global injectivity argument identified.

title: The bounded-degree almost sure period two conjecture for majority dynamics
statement: Let $G$ be an infinite graph of bounded degree, and choose the initial opinions independently and uniformly from $\{-1,1\}$. Under majority dynamics, each node's opinion almost surely converges to a cycle of period at most two. **Almost sure period two conjecture.** Every bounded-degree graph has the almost sure period two property. The conjecture extends the almost sure period two theorem for unimodular transitive graphs to all bounded-degree graphs. The paper gives an infinite counterexample without bounded degree, while the bounded-degree case is left open.
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Tie convention and update schedule omitted; source definition required.
technical_disposition: Universal bounded-degree infinite graph, iid fair initial spins, almost-sure eventual period at most two at each vertex. Finite-graph energy descent is not uniform on infinite graphs.

title: The conjecture that the equal-weight subgraph-count property is quasi-random
statement: Let $F$ be a graph with $e(F)>1$, and let $m=|F|$. For a graph property $\mathcal P(F;1/m,\dots,1/m)$ and its weaker version $\widetilde\mathcal P(F;1/m,\dots,1/m)$, the source context defines these as properties concerning equal-weight subgraph counts. **Equal-weight subgraph-count conjecture.** Theorem~ holds for any graph $F$ with $e(F)>1$; equivalently, $\mathcal P(F;1/m,\dots,1/m)$ and $\widetilde\mathcal P(F;1/m,\dots,1/m)$ are quasi-random properties for every such graph $F$. The conjecture extends the theorem proved for regular graphs, stars, and disconnected graphs; the only indicated counterexample is $F=K_2$, which has $e(F)=1$.

scope_flags: P and tilde-P not defined; Theorem~ is a broken reference.
technical_disposition: All F with more than one edge. Named counting properties and missing Theorem number prevent an exact quasirandomness implication from being reconstructed.

title: Polynomial-time computability of the maximum forcing number for elementary polyomino graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be an **elementary polyomino graph**, meaning that every edge of $G$ lies in some perfect matching.

**Xu et al.'s conjecture.** The maximum forcing number of $G$ can be computed in polynomial time.

The source says that this conjecture can now be confirmed, so the claim is a theorem rather than an open problem.

scope_flags: Maximum forcing definition absent in record, read in selected primary definitions; external LP theorem not independently replayed.
technical_disposition: Source Conjecture4.5 is explicitly confirmed by Theorem4.7 for all polyomino graphs with a perfect matching; elementary case is contained. Read reduction via elementary decomposition, Clar equality and LP theorem.

title: The explicit formula conjecture for Farey transfer-operator eigenfunctions
statement:
Let $q$ be a parameter and let $\mathbf{E}_{q}(y)$ denote the function introduced through the Farey transfer operators. For the previously considered cases $q=1$ and $q=\frac12$, one has $\mathbf{E}_{1}(y)=\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{\frac12}y$ and $\mathbf{E}_{1/2}(y)=y^{\frac12}$. **Explicit formula conjecture.** For all $q$,

$$
\mathbf{E}_{q}(y)=\left(\frac{2}{\pi}\right)^{q-\frac12}y^q.
$$

This extends the two explicitly verified cases and predicts a simple closed form for the functions arising from the Farey transfer operators. The supplied text gives no resolution of the assertion.
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: E_q and admissible analytic domain omitted in record; source y>0 and series definition read. No independent full dependency audit.
technical_disposition: v1 Appendix B conjecture is replaced in v3 Theorem B.2 by 2^(1/2-q)/Gamma(q+1/2) times y^q. Read complete local proof using Gegenbauer conversion and generating function. At q=3/2 coefficient 1/2 differs from 2/pi.

title: The bounded cohomology conjecture for smooth projective surfaces
statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective surface, and let $C$ be a curve on $X$. Write $h^i(\mathcal O_X(C))=\dim H^i(X,\mathcal O_X(C))$. The **bounded cohomology conjecture** asserts that there exists a positive constant $c_X$ such that

$$
h^1(\mathcal O_X(C))\le c_Xh^0(\mathcal O_X(C))
$$

for every curve $C$ on $X$. The conjecture is stronger than the bounded negativity conjecture and is the main conjecture studied in the paper. The source states that it implies bounded negativity, while the cited work disproves it by constructing a counterexample on a surface of general type.
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Record says curve; primary says prime divisor. Counterexample body in cited references not read; source citation alone is not proof-body clearance.
technical_disposition: For each smooth projective surface a single constant must control every integral curve. Primary Conj1.2 states prime-divisor version and explicitly cites existing counterexamples. Do not redevelop a known refutation.

title: Symmetry conjecture for crossing distributions of restricted permutations
statement:
Let $S_n^k$ denote the set of permutations in $S_n$ having the restriction indexed by $k$, and let ${\rm cr}(\sigma)$ be the number of crossings of a permutation $\sigma$. For an indeterminate $q$, define the crossing-distribution polynomial by

$$
\sum_{\sigma \in S_n^k} q^{{\rm cr}(\sigma)}.
$$

**Symmetry conjecture.** For all integers $n$ and $k$ satisfying $1\leq k\leq n$, we have

$$
\sum_{\sigma \in S_n^k} q^{{\rm cr}(\sigma)}=\sum_{\sigma \in S_n^{n+1-k}} q^{{\rm cr}(\sigma)}.
$$

The paper reports verification by computer up to $n=6$; the general identity is presented as a conjecture and no proof or resolution is supplied.
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Restriction indexed by k omitted. Selected v1 uses reverse-position-of-1 notation; record version not pinned. No inference from missing search match.
technical_disposition: Universal crossing-polynomial symmetry needs exact S_n^k definition. v1 has related cr-preserving rci and restricted bijections but inspected sections do not establish the asserted k versus n+1-k symmetry.

title: Higher-order modified Alder conjecture for a=3
statement:
Let $q_d^{(a)}(n)$ count partitions of $n$ into parts at least $a$ whose parts differ by at least $d$. For $1\leq b\leq d+2$, let $Q_d^{(b,-)}(n)$ count partitions of $n$ into parts congruent to $\pm b$ modulo $d+3$, excluding the part $d+3-b$, and define

$$
\Delta_d^{(a,b,-)}(n):=q_d^{(a)}(n)-Q_d^{(b,-)}(n),\qquad \Delta_d^{(a,-)}(n):=\Delta_d^{(a,a,-)}(n).
$$

**Higher-order modified Alder conjecture.** For all $d,n\geq 1$,

$$
\Delta_d^{(3,-)}(n)\geq 0.
$$

This is proposed as a generalization of Kang and Park's modified Alder conjecture to higher equal values of $a=b$. The source gives no proof or counterexample, so the assertion remains open.
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Definitions present and matched selected primary. Finite computation is diagnostic only.
technical_disposition: All d,n>=1, a=b=3. Read Conj1.4 and Prop4.1 proof: d multiple of3 in a large subrange only. Exact DP found no negative differences for d1..50,n1..400. Known injections do not bridge remaining all-d range.

title: A hyperbolic distance identity for intersections of lines in the Poincaré disk
statement:
Let $a,b,c,d$ be four complex points on the unit circle $S^1$ in this order, with the Euclidean lines $L(a,b)$ and $L(c,d)$ nonparallel. Let $h$ be an arbitrary point on the Euclidean segment $[b,c]$. Define

$$
g={\rm LIS}[a,b,c,d],\qquad j={\rm LIS}[g,h,a,c],\qquad k={\rm LIS}[g,h,b,d],\qquad l={\rm LIS}[g,h,a,d].
$$

Here ${\rm LIS}$ denotes the line-intersection construction used in the paper, and the special case $j=k$ is allowed. **Hyperbolic distance identity.** The hyperbolic distances in the Poincaré disk satisfy

$$
\rho_{\mathbb{B}^2}(h,j)=\rho_{\mathbb{B}^2}(k,l).
$$

This is a metric relation for the line-intersection construction associated with four cyclic points. The supplied text does not establish whether the statement is proved or remains open.
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Closed-segment endpoints put distances on boundary; degenerate intersections possible. Endpoint corrections get no credit. No new proof asserted.
technical_disposition: Read Conj5.10, LIS definition, preceding midpoint corollary/proof and Remark5.11 in v1 and corresponding v3 passage. Source already suggests Mobius normalization; full-scope algebra and successor clearance unestablished.

title: The second-smallest-value conjecture for the function $f$ on finite groups
statement: Let $f$ be the function on finite groups studied in the paper, with $f(G)=1$ precisely for cyclic groups. **Second-smallest-value conjecture.** $2$ is the second smallest value of the function $f$. This conjecture is motivated by the preceding lower bounds for non-cyclic groups and has been verified by computer for many classes of finite groups; its general validity remains open.

technical_disposition: Second-smallest value across all finite groups cannot be evaluated without literal definition and codomain of f; cyclic iff f=1 alone does not determine a gap.

title: The all-$k$ counterexample conjecture for dijoin additivity
statement:
For an integer $k\geq3$, let $T_k$ be a tournament and let $R$ be an oriented graph; $T_k\Rightarrow R$ denotes their dijoin, formed by adding all arcs from $T_k$ to $R$.

**The all-$k$ dijoin counterexample conjecture.** For any $k\geq3$, there is a tournament $T_k$ with $\operatorname{inv}(T_k)=k$ such that

$$
\operatorname{inv}(T_k\Rightarrow R)<k+\operatorname{inv}(R)
$$

for all $R$ with $\operatorname{inv}(R)\geq1$.

The paper proves this statement for every odd integer $k\geq3$ and conjectures that the same phenomenon holds for even integers. Thus the remaining content concerns even $k$.
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Inversion operation and inv are not defined in record.
technical_disposition: For every k>=3 one tournament must improve the dijoin bound for every R of positive inversion number. An isolated pair or odd-k construction does not settle even k.

title: Defant's linear-time conjecture for Pop-Stack Sorting on random permutations
statement:
Let $D70E_n$ be a uniformly random permutation in the symmetric group $D70E_n$, and let $D43E\operatorname{Pop}$ denote one step of Pop-Stack Sorting, which reverses every maximal decreasing run of a permutation. Write $D43E\operatorname{Id}_n$ for the identity permutation and let $o(1)$ tend to zero as $n\to\infty$. **Defant's conjecture.** Almost surely, Pop-Stack Sorting needs

$$
(1-o(1))n
$$

steps to reach $D43E\operatorname{Id}_n$ from $D70E_n$. This conjecture predicts a linear lower bound, asymptotically matching the trivial upper bound up to a vanishing factor; its resolution concerns the typical running time of Pop-Stack Sorting on a uniformly random permutation.
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: D70E_n and D43E are corrupt tokens; coupling/meaning of almost surely needs source.
technical_disposition: Typical asymptotic (1-o(1))n lower bound requires a high-probability obstruction surviving linearly many random-permutation passes. No short all-n route identified.

title: Nonexistence conjecture for {k, k}-equivelar wnp maps
statement: Let $K$ be a **wnp map**, meaning a polyhedral map attaining equality in the lower bound $n\geq (k-1)^2$ for an $n$-vertex $\{k,k\}$-equivelar polyhedral map. **Nonexistence conjecture.** There does not exist any $\{k,k\}$-equivelar wnp map for $k\geq 7$. This would extend the known nonexistence for $k=6$, where no 25-vertex $\{6,6\}$-equivelar polyhedral map exists, and would show that the lower bound is never attained for equal face and vertex degrees at least seven.
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Polyhedral map and wnp incidence conventions require primary definition.
technical_disposition: All k>=7 excludes extremal maps on (k-1)^2 vertices. Euler characteristic alone constrains genus but does not eliminate all such maps.

title: Fixed point proportion of dynamical exceptional polynomials
statement:
1. What can we say about the fixed-point proportion of groups acting on rooted trees?

2. Fixing the tree $T$, can we find a family of groups such that its fixed-point proportion is nonzero and its Hausdorff dimension converges to $1$?

3. What can we say about the fixed-point proportion of Galois groups?

4. What can we say about the fixed-point proportion of $IMG(f)$ of complex rational functions?

5. What can we say about the fixed-point proportion of $IMG(f)$ of complex polynomials that are not dynamically exceptional?

title: How does the group structure of the Brauer group relate to Brauer classes as obstructions to fineness of moduli spaces?

Given a K3 surface $X$ and two K3 surfaces $S_1$ and $S_2$ such that $X$ is a moduli space of sheaves on $S_1$ and $S_1$, can we explicitly construct a third K3 surface or variety $Y$ such that $X$ is a moduli space of sheaves on $Y$ and the obstruction class to fineness of this moduli space is the sum of the obstruction classes coming from $S_1$ and $S_2$?

statement: Consider $\mathbb{C}(u,v)=\mathbb{C}(\mathbb{P}^2)$. Does there exist a transcendence degree 1 subfield of $A$ (also a $\mathbb{C}$-subalgebra) which is not rational? title: Estimates for $\overline{\partial}$ (problem 5)
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a smooth bounded pseudoconvex domain such that for any $0<\eta<1$, there exists a defining function $\rho_{\eta}$ such that $-(-\rho_{\eta})^{\eta}$ is plurisubharmonic on $\Omega$. Note that such an $\eta$ always exists; however, it could be small. Determine minimal assumptions on $\Omega$ to show that $\overline{\partial}$-Neumann operator $N$ (or the Bergman projection operator $\mathbf{B}$) is globally regular. Are there any domains such that $\mathbf{B}$ is globally regular but no such a family of defining functions exists?

title: Spectral problems (problem 2)
statement:
Consider the domains

$$
\Omega_k = \left\{ (z,w) \in \mathbb{C}^{n+1} \colon \mathrm{Im}(w) < \lvert z\rvert^{2k} \right\}

and

$$
U_k = \left\{ (z,w) \in \mathbb{C}^{n+1} \colon \mathrm{Im}(w) < \sum_{j=1}^n \lvert z\rvert^{2k} \right\}.
$$

(a) Can one compute the spectrum of the Kohn Laplacian on $(0,1)$-forms in either case?

(b) Can one distinguish $\Omega_k$ from $U_k$ using the spectrum?

title: Homogeneisation of the Steklov-Neumann problem
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a domain in $\mathbb R^2$ and fix a fraction of the perimeter. Consider partitions of its boundary into $\Gamma = \Gamma_N \cup \Gamma_S$. Put Neumann boundary conditions on $\Gamma_N$ and Steklov on $\Gamma_S$. 

a) How should one separate the boundary to maximise the first non-zero eigenvalue?

b) What happens under homogeneisation?

c) What happens if one instead puts a weight on the boundary, i.e. amongst all functions $\rho$ on the boundary with fixed integal and value between $0$ and $1$, find the $\rho$ that optimises $\sigma_1$ in the eigenvalue problem

$$
\begin{cases} \Delta u = 0 \\ \frac{\partial u }{\partial n} = \sigma \rho u \end{cases}.
$$

title: 2-lift of Ramanujan graph
statement:
Is a random 2-lift of a Ramanujan graph also Ramanujan (or nearly) with constant probability? More precisely, let $G$ be a $d$-regular Ramanujan graph with adjacency matrix $A$. Construct the matrix $S$ by

$$
S_{ij} = \left\{\begin{array}{cl} 0 & \text{if } A_{ij} = 0 \\ \text{randomly } \pm 1 & \text{if } A_{ij} = 1. \end{array}\right.
$$

Is the spectral norm of $S$ less than $2\sqrt{d-1} + \epsilon$ with constant probability?

title: Distribution of Intersection Numbers of Undirected Graphs
statement: Given an undirected graph $G$, a clique of $G$ is an induced subgraph of $G$ that is complete (that is, any two distinct vetices are adjacent). An edge clique cover is a set of cliques covering all vertices of $G$. The intersection number of a graph $G$ is the number of cliques in a minimum edge-clique cover. Question: What is the distribution of these intersection numbers? If one were to make a histogram of all undirected graphs on $n$ vertices, what is the distribution of these intersection numbers?

statement: In the design of the hash function one has control over two parameters; the dimension of the special linear group considered, and the characteristic of the underlying field. We would like to determine appropriate choices for both via two branches of cryptanalysis: first, by analysis of the multivariate system implied by long matrix products; and second by direct analysis of group-theoretic properties. We should also study the impact of the partial homomorphicity exhibited by the scheme.

title: Nonlinear representation theory
statement:
Suppose we define an abstract notion of "wild nonabelian Hodge structure", consisting of a hyperkahler manifold with its various algebraic structures, such that it is a wild Hitchin moduli space for some choice of a group, an irregular curve and residue data. The choice of such a realisation of the abstract space can be viewed as a "representation" or "realisation" of the space. Study this representation theory.

Here we are viewing these moduli spaces as global/nonlinear analogues of algebraic groups (as the Riemann--Hilbert problem suggests).

For example, take one simple example (such as the $D_4$ Hitchin space, the Painleve VI space, $GL_2$ with four simple poles on $P^1$), of complex dimension $2$ and find all the possible representations of this space.

title: Geometric flows (problem 3)
statement:
Consider the flow of inverse Hermitian metrics on a compact complex manifold:

$$
\frac \partial {\partial t} g^{j \overline k} = g^{m \overline n} \partial_m \partial_{\overline n} g^{j \overline k} - \partial_m g^{j \overline k} \partial_{\overline n} g^{m \overline k}.
$$

One has short time existence, and it is known that at the maximal time of existence

$$
| \mathrm{Rm}^{\mathcal{Ch}} | + |T| + |\nabla T| \to \infty.
$$

Can this be improved? Can one find analogues of Perelman's $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal W$ functionals?
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Repeated/free indices in second term appear inconsistent; improvement criterion unspecified.
technical_disposition: Improve curvature/torsion blowup criterion or construct entropy functionals for inverse-Hermitian-metric flow. Needs tensorially well-defined PDE first.

title: For geodesic flows on non-compact metric spaces, can the variational principle have an extremal measure and metric?
statement:
For geodesic flows on non-compact metric spaces, can the variational principle have an extremal measure and metric? That is, if $\mathcal M_f$ is the set of $f$-invariant probability measures on $X$, $\mathcal D_X$ is the space of distances on $X$ inducing the same topology, $h_d(f) = \displaystyle \sup_{K \subset X} h_d(f,K)$ where the supremum is taken over the topological entropy of compact subsets $K$ with respect to the metric $d$, and:

$$
h_{\operatorname{Borel}}(f) & = & \sup_{\mu \in \mathcal M_f} h_\mu(f) \\ 
h_{\operatorname{top}}(f) & = & \inf_{d \in \mathcal D_X} h_{d}(f)
$$

The Borel and topological entropies were shown to coincide in for locally compact spaces. Under what conditions can one find a metric $d$ and measure $\mu$ which realize the common value?
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Map/geodesic-flow hypotheses and notion of compact-set entropy need source.
technical_disposition: Characterize simultaneous attainment of entropy infimum over compatible metrics and supremum over invariant measures on noncompact spaces. Compact examples are insufficient.

title: Rigidity (problem 6)
statement:
In L. Lovasz’s paper ["Flats in Matroids and geometric graphs”], he considers the dimension of $span(F\cap h)$, where $F$ is a family of linear subspaces of $R^d$, $h$ is a subspace of codimension 1 in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and $F\cap h:=\{f\cap h \mid f\in F\}$. He proves that this dimension can be expressed as a certain minimum over all the partitions of the elements of $F$, given that $h$ satisfies a certain "general position” assumption. The questions are:

(i) Can the general position assumption in Lovasz’s theorem be relaxed?

(ii) Can one find a formula (in whatever terms) that applies to subspaces $h$ that are not necessarily in general position?
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Lovasz genericity condition and meaning of span of family not stated fully; routine rank calculation earns no credit.
technical_disposition: For arbitrary hyperplane the dimension can be computed by linear algebra, but a partition-formula extension/relaxed general-position criterion needs exact requested format.

title: Gradient Estimate
statement:
Consider the equation

$$
F[\lambda[u]]=\psi,
$$

where $\omega_{0},\omega_{X}$ are nonnegative Hermitian $(1,1)$-forms
and $\lambda[u]$ are the eigenvalues of $\omega_{0}+\sqrt{-1}\partial\overline{\partial}u$
with respect to $\omega_{X}$. Assume the $C$-subsolution condition
holds, and that $F$ is concave. Is it possible to prove effective
estimates (not through a contradiction argument) of the form

$$
\sup_{X}|\nabla u|\leq C(\omega_{0},\omega_{X},\psi,F)?
$$

For example, can one prove this using maximum principle techniques? 

Blocki did this for the complex Monge-Ampere equation using maximum
principle techniques, but so far there is no known direct proof in
the case of the $\sigma_{k}$ equations. It is also known in the case
of deformed Hermitian-Yang-Mills.
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Positive reference metric, normalization, ellipticity cone and subsolution dependence absent.
technical_disposition: Effective gradient estimate for concave Hessian equation with C-subsolution requires uniform quantitative ellipticity/subsolution controls. Maximum-principle analogy alone not a proof.

title: The Problems (problem 6)
statement:
Let $X$ be a Hilbert modular surface over ${\\mathbb{Q}}$. All of the Tate classes that arise from modular curves on $X$ are defined over ${\\mathbb{Q}}^{ab}$; however, there also exist Tate classes which are algebraic, but not defined over ${\\mathbb{Q}}^{ab}$. (In fact, they are defined over dihedral extensions of ${\\mathbb{Q}}$.) We know the algebraicity of these classes, but do not know specific representatives.

Comments:

1. One possible suggestion for such representatives could be non-congruence curves on $X$. (D. Ramakrishnan)

2. If we can find representatives, we can intersect them with the modular curves: this may be a way to find interesting non-Heegner points on the modular curves. (D. Ramakrishnan)
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Surface/level and class not specified; rationality alone does not choose explicit cycles.
technical_disposition: Explicit algebraic representatives for non-abelian-defined Tate classes on Hilbert modular surfaces require descent and cohomological identification.

title: The Problems (problem 18)
statement: Let $E$ be an elliptic curve over ${\\mathbb{Q}}$ with CM by $K$ and with associated Hecke character $\chi$. Then $\chi^2$ is associated to a modular form of weight 3 appearing in $H^2(\mathcal E)$, $\mathcal E\to X$ for a modular curve $X$ (whose level is the norm of the conductor of $\chi^2$ times the discriminant of $K$). The Tate and Hodge Conjectures predict the existence of a correspondence $E\times E\to \mathcal E$ because the same motive appears in $H^2$ of both sides. Can we exhibit this correspondence explicitly?
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Exact modular model and correspondence coefficients/field omitted.
technical_disposition: Explicit correspondence between CM E times E and elliptic modular surface must realize the identified motive. Matching L-factors alone is insufficient.

title: Moduli height
statement:
Let $X$ be a quasi-projective variety and $G$ a group action on $X$. Let $Y=X//G$ be a geometric quotient of $X$ by $G$. Is $h_Y(x) \asymp \min_{g \in G} h_X(gx)$? (ample heights)

 In particular, fix an embedding $M_d \subset \mathbb{P}^M$. Then define a height $h_M:M_d \to {\\mathbb{R}}$ using the embedding. Is this height function comparable to the minimum height of the maps in the class in $\mathop{Rat}_d$?
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Base field, multiplicative/additive heights and min versus inf not specified.
technical_disposition: Height comparison on general quotient requires coherent heights, properness and orbit minimum conventions; special moduli-of-maps case is a separate scope.

title: Can one find a version of the recipe using asymmetric approximate functional equations, giving a “robust” version of the calculations?
statement:
Can one find a version of the recipe using asymmetric approximate functional equations, giving a “robust” version of the calculations? Similarly, can one apply the Conrey-Keating method using two asymmetric Dirichlet polynomials

$$
\sum_{m\leq X} \frac{\tau_A(m)}{m^s} \ \ \ \ \ \ \text{and} \ \ \ \ \ \ 
\sum_{n\leq Y} \frac{\tau_B(n)}{n^{1-s}}
$$

to get the same answer as before, i.e. when $X=Y$?
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Recipe, A,B, allowed X,Y regime and same answer undefined.
technical_disposition: Asymmetric approximate-functional-equation/Dirichlet-polynomial recipes need exact original conjectural moment formula before equality of outputs is meaningful.

title: Complexity (problem 1)
statement:
Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and let $G$ be an ordered divisible group. Consider the Hahn field, defined as follows:

$$
K((G)) = \left\{\sum_{g\in S}a_g t^g \mid S\subseteq G \text{ well-ordered}, a_g\in K\right\}
$$

If $K$ and $G$ are computable and $f\in K((G))[X]$, how complex is it to determine a root of $f$?
At each step, the procedure should produce the next term in a root of $f$, based on the $a_g$ in the input coefficients of $f$. For each step $\alpha$, how many jumps over these coefficients are needed to do step $\alpha$?
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Computable presentations/support access and ordinal notation system unspecified.
technical_disposition: Transfinite root-term computation in computable Hahn fields asks jump complexity at every ordinal stage; algebraic closedness does not give effective support oracle bounds.

title: Problems related to Xiao-Zhu (problem 1)
statement: Consider Xiao-Zhu specialized to Tate classes associated to Hilbert modular forms at an inert prime. In the generic case, i.e. when the Satake parameters are different, then there is a 2-dimensional space of Tate classes, and Xiao-Zhu produce a 2-dimensional space of cycles. In the nongeneric case the dimension of Tate classes is $4$, and Xiao-Zhu produce only 1 cycle. Can you find extra cycles when the Satake parameters are equal? More generally, in non-generic cases of Xiao-Zhu, can you construct the missing cycles?
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Exact Shimura/level and equal-parameter assumptions omitted; source framework needed.
technical_disposition: Construct missing cycles for repeated Satake parameters in Xiao-Zhu requires nongeneric geometric correspondence; dimension difference alone is not construction.

title: Relationship between Trivial delta method and Nelson's Kernel method
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Kernel bump and normalizations undefined; z,x versus z,w notation inconsistent.
technical_disposition: Precise relation of two subconvex methods requires explicit kernel and transforms matching both analytic estimates. Shared Burgess exponent not an equivalence proof.

title: Similar to Kudla program, we could also define a generating series of (derived) complex multiplication cycles on Shimura varieties and conjecture its modularity.
statement: Similar to Kudla program, we could also define a generating series of (derived) complex multiplication cycles on Shimura varieties and conjecture its modularity. Is it possible to compute arithmetic intersection of the generating series with special divisors / Hodge bundle and prove its numerical modularity when the Shimura variety has low dimension e.g. on Siegel threefold or Hilbert modular surface?
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Series/coefficient and intersection regularization data absent.
technical_disposition: Modularity and intersection of derived CM generating series in low-dimensional Shimura varieties require defining cycles and arithmetic product first.

title: Computing Fourier coefficients from $L$-values
statement:
Let $d$ be a positive integer and let $F$ be a Siegel modular form with Fourier coefficients $a(F)$. In many cases, we know the (generalized) B\"{o}cherer conjecture:

$$
\left \lvert \sum_{S \in \mathrm{Cl}_d} a(F, S) \Lambda(S) \right \rvert^2 = L\big(\pi_F \times \theta_\Lambda, \frac{1}{2}\big) = L\big(\mathrm{BC}_{K/\mathbb{Q}} (\pi_F) \times \Lambda, \frac{1}{2}\big).
$$

Knowing this equality and values of $L(\pi_F \times \theta_\Lambda, \frac{1}{2})$ for many $\Lambda$, can we compute the Fourier coefficients $a(F, S)$?
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Normalization constants, class group and whether F fixed up to scalar unspecified; source parked.
technical_disposition: Squared character-transform magnitudes leave global phase/sign ambiguous; Fourier inversion requires phase information, not just these L-values. This obstruction does not settle reconstruction with all automorphic constraints.

title: There were several questions proposed around this, including What should the predicted values of … be?
statement:
There were several questions proposed around this, including

* What should the predicted values of $a,b,c$ be?

* What is the "shape" of the set $U$ that one should take? In the usual Manin conjecture, one expects that $U$ can be taken to be the complement of a thin set.

* Can one compute asymptotics for $N_{X,\mathscr L}(U,B;d)$ if $X=\mathbb P^2_{\mathbb Q}$ and $d=3$, for some choices of $\mathscr L$?
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Literal fragment refers to this and U with no preceding definitions; incomplete non-self-contained record.
technical_disposition: Requested exponents a,b,c and asymptotics for degree3 points on P2 cannot be evaluated without counting function/height/open-set definitions.

title: Examples of MCG-finite irreducible representations of surface groups not arising from abelian varieties
statement:
Can we find an examples of an irreducible representation $\rho: \pi_1(\Sigma_{g,n}) \to {\\textrm{GL}}_r(\mathbb{C})$ with finite orbit under $\mathrm{Mod}(\Sigma_{g,n})$ that do not arise from families of abelian varieties? 

We say that a representation “arises from a family of abelian varieties” if there exists a complex structure on $S = \Sigma_{g,n}$ such that there is an Zariski open $U \subset S$ and a family of abelian varities $A \to U$ such that the representation restricted to $U$ is a subquotient of the Gauss-Manin local system of $A \to U$.
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Genus/puncture/rank range not quantified; finite image alone is not demonstrated outside abelian origin.
technical_disposition: Existence of finite-MCG-orbit irreducible representation outside abelian-variation subquotients needs monodromy and Hodge-origin obstruction simultaneously.

title: Moments of derivatives
statement:
What do the methods for computing moments of L function give if one tries to
compute moments of derivatives.
Even in the random matrix theory setting computing the distribution of
derivatives is difficult.
What can recent methods tell us about the distribution of values of derivatives
of $L$ functions?
This structure is related to the Painlev\'e V equation, and the moment (for
finite $n$) is a polynomial in $N$, the size of the random matrix.
Also, they correspond to solutions for Painlev\'e III as $n \to \infty$.
record_statement_review: literal supplied statement read in full including displayed quantifiers
scope_flags: Family, derivative order, scaling, moment and Painleve normalization omitted.
technical_disposition: Requests moment/distribution information about L-function derivatives; finite-N random-matrix polynomial observation is not a specified universal conjecture.
